paper_title: Constraints on axion-like polarization oscillations in the cosmic microwave background with POLARBEAR
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling constant
notes: Paper reports a median 95% upper limit on axion-photon coupling g_agamma < (2.4 × 10^-11 GeV^-1) × (m_a / 10^-21 eV) over the mass range 9.6 × 10^-22 eV to 2.2 × 10^-20 eV. This is the stochastic case where the axion field amplitude is treated as a Rayleigh-distributed random variable (following Ref. [22]), which is more appropriate than the deterministic case when the experiment timescale is much shorter than the axion coherence time (~6000 years). The limit assumes the axion constitutes all dark matter with local density ρ_0 = 0.3 GeV/cm^3. The constraint is derived from a search for sinusoidal oscillations in CMB polarization angle measured by POLARBEAR over two observing seasons (2012-2016). No signal was detected (p-value = 0.048, 1.7σ). The frequency range 0.02-0.45 days^-1 corresponds to oscillation periods from ~2 to ~50 days, limited by HWP position uncertainty at longer periods. The constraint assumes a stochastic local axion field amplitude with Rayleigh-distributed phase. The mass range probed is 9.6×10^-22 eV ≤ m_a ≤ 2.2×10^-20 eV, corresponding to oscillation periods from ~100 days to ~0.1 days. The median bound is g_agamma < (2.4×10^-11 GeV^-1) × (m_a/10^-21 eV).
